title: People v. Sandiganbayan (Desierto)
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the discretion of the Ombudsman in finding probable cause for violations of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. The Ombudsman's determination of probable cause is generally not subject to judicial review unless there is grave abuse of discretion.
doctrine: The determination of probable cause during preliminary investigation is an executive function. Courts generally do not interfere with the Ombudsman's exercise of this power unless there is a clear showing of grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction.
fullText:
CARPIO, J.:

The issue is whether the Sandiganbayan committed grave abuse of discretion in dismissing the information for violation of Section 3(e) of RA 3019.

The determination of probable cause during a preliminary investigation is an executive function. The Ombudsman is vested with the power to investigate and prosecute cases involving public officials. The Court has consistently held that it will not interfere with the Ombudsman's exercise of his investigatory and prosecutory powers absent a clear showing of grave abuse of discretion.
